newsitem.title: UK: S.Africa plans 2nd Yankee for min 20 years-dealers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans 2nd Yankee for min 20 years-dealers.

text.p: South Africa could launch its second Yankee bond soon after inviting bids for the mandate last week, syndicate officials said on Monday.
They said a $400 to $500 million 20-year bond was expected, although a longer maturity of 30 years was also possible.
It would be the country's longest maturity issue in the international bond market following 10-year deals in dollars and sterling last year.
One source said some investors had suggested a 100-year maturity as China had such a deal outstanding.
"But I don't think they're seriously looking at it." Pricing was vague. "I wouldn't put a number out there," said one. "It will depend on market conditions."
Another trader said a broad range of between 190 and 210 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes was expected.
"But we expect it at the tighter end of this range," he said.
Last week investment banks were invited to bid for the mandate and a decision on the winner is expected this week, dealers said.
The country is also eyeing its second Samurai issue, dealers said.
Market sources said a maturity longer than its previous five-year issue was likely, either at seven or 10 years.
In October last year, South Africa launched a $300 million 10-year Yankee via Merrill Lynch.
The bond was priced to yield 195 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and was last trading tighter at around 160 b.p, traders said.
The country is rated Baa3 by Moody's Investors Service and BB+ by Standard & Poor's.
